## Reproducing this session

This folder is self-contained: everything below works from `final_report/` alone, with no
access to the original session workspace or this conversation.

### 1. Copy this folder and set the one required path

```bash
cp -r final_report/ /path/to/scratch/ray_molformer_repro
cd /path/to/scratch/ray_molformer_repro
```

Edit `config.ini` and set `WORKSPACE_ROOT` to wherever you want this reproduction to live
(any writable directory — it does NOT need to match the original session's path). This is the
ONLY file where a real path goes; every script under `scripts/` sources it via
`scripts/lib_load_config.sh` instead of hardcoding one. Optionally also set `OUTPUT_ROOT` if you
want run output kept separate from `WORKSPACE_ROOT` itself (defaults to the same directory).

```ini
WORKSPACE_ROOT=/path/to/scratch/ray_molformer_repro/ws
```

### 2. Rebuild the app + dftracer

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

This clones the app (from `APP_REPO_URL`/`APP_REF` in `config.ini`), builds dftracer into a
fresh venv, and installs the app's own Python dependencies (Ray 2.48.0, PyTorch/ROCm, RDKit) —
see `scripts/install.sh` itself for the exact pip/module commands this session actually used.

### 3. Run each case, in order

Requires a live Flux allocation on a Ray-capable ROCm system (this session ran on Tuolumne,
AMD MI300A, 2-4 nodes). Pass your allocation id as the one argument:

```bash
bash scripts/run_all.sh <your-flux-allocation-id>
```

This runs, in sequence:
- `scripts/baseline_runner.sh` — 2-node/8-GPU baseline, fp32, real 5000-row PubChem dataset + RDKit descriptors (see REPORT.md §2)
- `scripts/opt1_runner.sh` — 2-node/8-GPU, bf16 autocast forward pass (REPORT.md §7 row 1, §7c)
- `scripts/opt1_4node_runner.sh` — same opt1 code, scaled to 4-node/16-GPU (REPORT.md §7b)

To run a single case instead of the whole ladder (e.g. to re-check just opt1):

```bash
flux proxy <your-flux-allocation-id> bash scripts/opt1_runner.sh
```

(`flux run` alone queues a NEW job instead of using your existing allocation — always go through
`flux proxy <alloc>` as shown, both here and in `run_all.sh`.)

### 4. Verify it reproduced

Compare your printed Job Time / iteration timings against `REPORT.md` §7 (Optimization Ledger)
and §7b (N-Way Comparator Table):

| Config | Expected Job Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | 265.4s (or ~40s if measuring the training-loop-only phase, per REPORT.md §7 footnote) | |
| opt1 (bf16) | 262-275s | flat-to-slightly-slower than baseline is the EXPECTED result, not a bug — see REPORT.md §7 row 1 |
| opt1 4-node | ~310s | slower than opt1 2-node is EXPECTED — see REPORT.md §7 row 10 |

This is a live shared HPC system, so expect variation of roughly ±10% run to run — anything
within that band should be read as "reproduced," not as a discrepancy. If your numbers are
wildly different (e.g. an order of magnitude off, or `torch.autocast` errors), first check
`scripts/opt1_runner.sh`'s exported env vars against your system's actual NIC/ROCm setup rather
than assuming the code itself regressed.

### 5. Regenerate the PDF or re-check this README, standalone

```bash
bash scripts/render_pdf.sh          # REPORT.md -> REPORT.pdf
bash scripts/readme_smoke_test.sh   # checks this README still names every script/step
```
